outside ``modules``/``properties`` would teach the wrong thing even if the
runtime rejected it.

test_functions.name: test_parameter_patterns_are_the_schema_patterns_with_an_ecma_anchor
test_functions.doc:
The anchor differs on purpose, and only the anchor may differ.

``docs/ctam/schema/`` is validated by this repo's Python walker, so those
patterns end in ``\Z``. This document is also read by OpenAPI tooling, whose
regex dialect has no ``\Z``, so its inline patterns end in ``$``. That makes
two spellings of the same constraint, which is exactly the drift
``test_repeated_patterns_are_identical_across_schemas`` guards inside the
schema directory and cannot see across the boundary.

Requiring every inline pattern to be a checked-in schema pattern with the
anchor swapped keeps the pair in step, and fails if someone copies a pattern
into a schema file without re-anchoring it.

test_functions.name: test_table_covers_every_verdict
test_functions.doc: A table that lost all its HOST rows would still pass every row below.

test_functions.name: test_schema_pattern_verdict
test_functions.doc:
The pattern rejects exactly the SCHEMA rows and admits the rest.

A HOST row passing here is the expected, documented state, not a gap that
slipped through: the pattern has no way to know what the caller owns.

test_functions.name: test_host_rows_are_all_inside_the_two_containers
test_functions.doc:
Ownership is the only thing left to decide for a HOST row.

If a HOST row were outside ``modules``/``properties``, it would mean the
pattern had a hole in container enforcement, which is the one thing it is
responsible for.

test_functions.name: test_traversal_segment_is_a_literal_key
test_functions.doc:
Pins the reasoning behind the ``..`` row so it is not 'fixed' by mistake.

Rejecting ``..`` in the pattern would be treating a JSON Pointer as a
filesystem path, which is the confusion the plan warns about. The segment is
a legal key name; the requirement is that the host never resolves it
positionally.

test_functions.name: test_expected_schema_set_is_present
test_functions.doc: Guards the parametrization: a silently empty glob would pass everything.

test_functions.name: test_schema_parses_and_uses_only_supported_keywords
test_functions.doc:
The walker rejects unknown keywords, so an author cannot reach for $ref.

``_check_supported_keywords`` is the real gate used at config load time.
Running it here means a schema that would blow up at startup fails in CI
instead.

test_functions.name: test_no_unsupported_keyword_anywhere
test_functions.doc:
Broader than ``_check_supported_keywords``, which only recurses into
``properties``, ``additionalProperties``, and ``items``.

A subschema reached any other way would escape that check, so scan every
dict that looks like a schema and confirm it too is clean.

test_functions.name: test_every_pattern_compiles_and_is_anchored
test_functions.doc:
Patterns must end in ``\Z``, not ``$``.

The walker matches with ``re.search`` (loader.py:410), not ``re.fullmatch``,
so anchoring is the author's job. Python's ``$`` also matches immediately
before a trailing newline, which means a ``$``-anchored pattern accepts a
value with a trailing newline. ``"\\S"`` is the sanctioned exception: it is
a non-emptiness check, not a format check, and must not be anchored.

test_functions.name: test_dollar_anchor_admits_a_trailing_newline
test_functions.doc:
Freezes the reason the previous test exists.

Uses the shipped pointer pattern with only the anchor swapped, so this
demonstrates the actual hole rather than a contrived one. The segment class
already excludes control characters; ``$`` lets the newline through anyway by
matching in front of it. If a future Python made ``$`` behave like ``\Z``,
this test fails and the anchoring rule can be relaxed deliberately rather
than by accident.

test_functions.name: test_repeated_patterns_are_identical_across_schemas
test_functions.doc:
No ``$ref`` means shared shapes are copied, so drift is the failure mode.

Group every pattern by the field name it constrains and require one distinct
source per name. Without this, ``analysis_time`` could tighten in one schema
and stay loose in another with nothing to notice.

test_functions.name: test_timestamp_pattern_rejects_a_naive_timestamp
test_functions.doc:
An explicit offset is required everywhere a time appears.

This is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: StormCast currently falls back to
a naive ``datetime.now()``, so a naive value is a real thing that can reach
the boundary and it must be rejected there.

test_functions.name: test_string_length_cannot_be_bounded_by_keyword
test_functions.doc:
Records a real limitation of the restricted set.

``minLength``/``maxLength`` are absent, so length bounds are folded into
patterns as quantifiers. If a future author adds ``minLength`` expecting it
to work, ``_check_supported_keywords`` raises, and this test explains why.

test_functions.name: test_number_type_rejects_non_finite_values
test_functions.doc:
``type: number`` gets finiteness for free (loader.py:335-340).

The plan requires finite JSON values in patches. This confirms where that is
already enforced, and ``test_patch_value_finiteness_is_not_enforced`` marks
where it is not.

test_functions.name: test_patch_value_finiteness_is_not_enforced_by_schema
test_functions.doc:
A non-finite number nested in a patch value passes the schema.

``value`` is arbitrary JSON, so the walker has no subschema to recurse with.
The plan's finite-value rule must therefore be enforced in host code. This
test exists so that requirement is not quietly assumed to be covered.

test_functions.name: test_a_loose_file_beside_the_module_directories_is_skipped
test_functions.doc:
A README or a tarball in the module root is not a candidate.

``iterdir`` yields it, so the directory check has to be explicit or a stray
download becomes an invalid module.

test_functions.name: test_an_invalid_manifest_is_reported_not_dropped
test_functions.doc:
The regression this whole module replaces: a module disappearing quietly.

An operator who mistyped a key needs the parse error surfaced against the
directory they edited, not a shorter module list they have to notice.

test_functions.name: test_an_invalid_manifest_keeps_its_directory_name_as_the_reported_id
test_functions.doc:
With no parsed manifest there is no declared id, so the folder is the id.

Without this the reason would have nothing to name and an operator could not
tell which of several broken directories failed.

test_functions.name: test_a_semantically_invalid_manifest_reports_the_validation_message
test_functions.doc:
The manifest rule text is what discovery publishes, verbatim.

A generic "invalid manifest" would force the operator to reproduce the parse
by hand to learn which key was wrong.

test_functions.name: test_a_disabled_module_keeps_its_manifest
test_functions.doc:
An operator listing modules wants the version of the thing they turned off.

Discarding the manifest would make a disabled module indistinguishable from a
broken one in the status record.

test_functions.name: test_a_disabled_module_is_not_runnable
test_functions.doc: ``runnable`` is the launch list, so a disabled module must not appear in it.

test_functions.name: test_case_insensitive_id_collision_invalidates_both_directories
test_functions.doc:
Naming both is fixable; picking a winner is what silently lost a module.

Ids are compared case-insensitively downstream (output keys, status records),
so ``cellstats`` and ``CellStats`` cannot coexist -- and neither of them gets
to be the one that survives.

test_functions.name: test_after_naming_an_uninstalled_module_is_invalid
test_functions.doc:
Launching anyway would run the module without the input it declared.

"Not installed" is an operator action -- install it or drop the line -- so it
has to be named in the reason rather than inferred from an ordering failure.

test_functions.name: test_after_naming_a_disabled_module_is_invalid_and_says_so
test_functions.doc:
Disabling one module must not silently degrade another that depends on it.

The reason has to distinguish "disabled" from "missing", because the fix is
different: flip a flag versus install a package.

test_functions.name: test_after_naming_an_invalid_module_is_invalid
test_functions.doc:
A dependent of a broken module cannot run, and should not look like it can.

The reason points at the module to fix first so the operator does not chase
the symptom.

test_functions.name: test_invalidity_propagates_transitively
test_functions.doc:
A dependent two hops from the real fault must not be admitted.

Without the fixed-point loop, ``alpha`` sees a ``beta`` that is still
``discovered`` on the first pass, looks runnable, and fails at launch time
instead of at discovery.

test_functions.name: test_a_two_module_cycle_invalidates_both_and_names_the_cycle
test_functions.doc:
A cycle has no correct order, so no member may run and all must be named.

Reporting only one member would send the operator to edit the module that is
not necessarily the one with the wrong ``after`` line.

test_functions.name: test_a_three_module_cycle_invalidates_every_member
test_functions.doc:
Cycle detection must not be a two-node special case.

A longer cycle is the realistic one -- nobody writes ``a after b, b after a``
on purpose -- and it is the case a naive pairwise check misses.

test_functions.name: test_depending_on_the_builtin_stormcast_is_legal_and_adds_no_member
test_functions.doc:
Every cell module that consumes forecasts declares ``after = ["stormcast"]``.

``stormcast`` is the built-in adapter, so it must satisfy the dependency
without appearing in the result as an installed module that discovery could
then report on, order, or count against capacity.

test_functions.name: test_a_dependency_chain_runs_in_dependency_order
test_functions.doc:
``after`` is the only ordering control a module author has.

Alphabetically the chain here is exactly backwards, so an id-only sort would
run each module before the one it declared it must follow.

test_functions.name: test_independent_modules_come_out_in_ascending_id_order
test_functions.doc:
With no ``after`` edges the id is the only stable tiebreak available.

Falling back on directory iteration order would make the run sequence, and
therefore any ordering-sensitive bug, depend on the filesystem.

test_functions.name: test_order_is_a_function_of_the_graph_and_the_ids_alone
test_functions.doc:
Two identical installations built in opposite orders must run identically.

``after`` is a partial order, so a comparison sort over it returns whatever
the input sequence suggested. Pinning the two roots against each other is
what catches that, because either order looks reasonable in isolation.

test_functions.name: test_modules_past_the_cap_are_invalid_and_still_reported
test_functions.doc:
The cap bounds discovery and status work; it must not hide the overflow.

An operator who installs one module too many needs to be told which one was
refused, so the cap is applied by demoting the tail rather than truncating
the list.

test_functions.name: test_capacity_is_applied_after_ordering_not_in_directory_order
test_functions.doc:
Which module is dropped is a property of the graph, not of folder names.

``zzz`` sorts last but every other module depends on it, so the dependency
order puts it near the front and it is admitted; the module demoted is one
that sorts *earlier*. Applying the cap over the scan order instead would drop
``zzz`` and leave its dependents pointing at a refused module.

test_functions.name: test_invalid_and_disabled_modules_do_not_consume_capacity
test_functions.doc:
A module that will never launch must not push a working one over the cap.

Otherwise disabling a module would reduce, not increase, the number of
modules that actually run.

test_functions.name: test_a_symlinked_module_directory_pointing_outside_the_root_is_invalid
test_functions.doc:
The module root is the trust boundary an operator actually administers.

Following a symlink out of it would let anything writable elsewhere on the
box install a module, so the escape is recorded rather than traversed.

test_functions.name: test_discovered_module_is_frozen
test_functions.doc:
A verdict is a record of what discovery decided, not mutable state.

Later phases attach runtime state elsewhere; letting them retouch ``state``
here would make the status record disagree with the discovery decision.

test_functions.name: test_discovery_result_is_frozen
test_functions.doc: The scan is a snapshot; a caller must re-scan rather than edit the result.

test_functions.name: test_runnable_is_a_filtered_view_in_the_same_order
test_functions.doc: Callers launch from ``runnable``, so it has to preserve dependency order.

test_functions.doc: 128 is the quantifier boundary of the frozen module_id pattern.

indistinguishable to an operator reading a snapshot and to anything that
lower-cases a lookup.

test_functions.name: test_non_three_part_version_is_rejected
test_functions.doc: The status record records ``version`` under ``^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\Z``.

test_functions.name: test_boolean_timeout_is_rejected_despite_bool_being_an_int
test_functions.doc:

``timeout_seconds = true`` would then pass as 1 second and silently give the
module the minimum budget instead of failing the manifest.

test_functions.name: test_shell_string_entrypoint_is_rejected
test_functions.doc: An argument vector, never a shell string: the launcher uses no shell.

test_functions.name: test_shell_metacharacter_in_an_argument_is_rejected
test_functions.doc:

Phase 4 should never have to decide whether ``main.py; rm -rf /`` was meant
as one filename or two commands.

test_functions.name: test_symlinked_entrypoint_pointing_outside_the_module_directory_is_rejected
test_functions.doc:
``resolve()`` is what makes containment survive a symlink, not string checks.

``payload.py`` looks contained and is not, which is exactly the case a
prefix comparison on the unresolved path would admit.

test_functions.name: test_flag_arguments_are_not_treated_as_paths
test_functions.doc: A flag is not a payload, so containment must not reject ``--config``.

test_functions.name: test_self_reference_in_after_is_rejected
test_functions.doc: A self-dependency is a cycle of length one and would deadlock ordering.

test_functions.name: test_family_is_folded_to_lowercase_while_raw_is_preserved
test_functions.doc:
The case asymmetry is deliberate and comes from the Phase 0 examples.

The selector spells the family in the plan's uppercase form
(``input:MRMS:...``) while a catalog ``file_id`` uses lowercase
(``input:mrms:...``), so ``family`` is folded for matching. ``raw`` stays
verbatim because ``requirements-evaluation.schema.json`` requires the
selector to be echoed back exactly as the manifest wrote it.

test_functions.name: test_product_case_is_not_folded
test_functions.doc: Product ids are mixed case in the catalog, so folding would break matching.

test_functions.name: test_alerts_selector_is_rejected_with_an_explanation
test_functions.doc: Alerts are deliberately not an admitted Phase 1 input, not an oversight.

test_functions.name: test_product_typo_fails_at_discovery_against_the_host_catalog
test_functions.doc: A typo must not become a requirement that is perpetually unsatisfied.

test_functions.name: test_selector_violating_the_frozen_pattern_is_rejected
test_functions.doc: The frozen selector pattern admits no space, so a spaced product fails.

test_functions.name: test_selector_with_a_trailing_newline_is_rejected
test_functions.doc: ``\Z`` rather than ``$``: Python's ``$`` also matches before a newline.

test_functions.name: test_max_age_on_a_host_owned_selector_is_rejected
test_functions.doc:
Host artifacts are always this cycle's, so freshness there is meaningless.

Accepting the key would give the author a false sense that staleness was
being checked on something that has no staleness.

test_functions.name: test_min_history_entries_above_the_read_window_is_a_manifest_bug
test_functions.doc:
No read can return more than the maximum window, so this can never pass.

Recording it as an unmet runtime requirement every cycle would hide an
authoring mistake behind a recurring operational alarm.

test_functions.name: test_manifest_with_no_writes_is_rejected
test_functions.doc: A module that declares no output has nothing to contribute.

test_functions.name: test_the_same_pointer_under_two_resources_is_not_a_duplicate
test_functions.doc: Uniqueness is per ``(resource, pointer)``: the two documents differ.

test_functions.name: test_control_character_in_a_pointer_segment_is_rejected
test_functions.doc: A NUL or newline cannot be written into a TOML literal, so build it directly.

test_functions.name: test_traversal_segment_is_rejected_as_a_literal_key_not_as_a_path
test_functions.doc:
``..`` is a legal JSON Pointer key name, and that is exactly why it fails.

``/features/*/modules/CellStats/../id`` must be read as the four keys
``modules``, ``CellStats``, ``..``, ``id``. Under that reading it is accepted
on ownership grounds -- it is a deep key inside the caller's own namespace.
The dangerous reading is the filesystem one, where the pointer collapses to
``/id``. So the case the host must get right is the *sibling* form
``/features/*/modules/../id``, which names a key ``..`` under ``modules``
that the caller does not own. It is rejected for not being the owner's key,
not for containing dots. See ``plans/modular-ctam-phase0-findings.md``
section 10.

test_functions.name: test_pointer_segment_is_unescaped_exactly_once
test_functions.doc:
``~01`` must decode to the literal ``~1``, never on to ``/``.

Unescaping ``~0`` before ``~1``, or unescaping twice, would invent a
separator the author never wrote and split one owned key into two.

test_functions.name: test_encoded_separator_cannot_smuggle_a_container_name
test_functions.doc:
``/features/*/modules~1CellStats`` is one key, and it is not a container.

A string-prefix check on the raw pointer would see ``modules`` and admit it.
